scholarships.title: Erasmus Mundus Joint Masters Degrees (EMJMD/EMJM) Scholarships

existing.description: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degrees are integrated international master's programmes jointly delivered by at least three higher education institutions from at least three different countries, at least two of which are EU Member States or Programme-associated third countries. The European Commission funds the programmes and offers EU scholarships to the best-ranked students worldwide at EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months. Students apply directly to the institution running their chosen programme, usually between October and January for entry the following academic year.
eligibility: Hold a bachelor's degree (first degree), or be in the last year of bachelor's studies
Graduate before the master's programme starts
Alternatively demonstrate a bachelor's equivalent level of learning, officially recognised according to national legislation and practices in the degree-awarding country
Students from all over the world are welcome; individual consortia publish further entry requirements
Note: students who previously obtained an EMJM scholarship are not eligible for an additional EMJM scholarship
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must hold a bachelor's degree (first degree) or be in the final year of bachelor's studies, and must graduate before the master's programme starts. Applicants may apply with a demonstrably equivalent level of learning if it is officially recognised in the degree-awarding country. Students from all over the world are eligible, and each master's website lists its own entry requirements.
benefits: EU scholarship of EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months
Coverage of participation costs, travel and visa costs
Joint degree or multiple degrees from an international consortium of at least three institutions in at least three countries
coverage: Participation costs of the master's programme (consortia cannot charge tuition fees or other mandatory participation costs to Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders)
Living allowance of EUR 1,400 per month for a maximum of 24 months
requirements: Search the official Erasmus Mundus course catalogue for the latest selected programmes
Apply directly to the institution running the chosen programme
Submit the application within the consortium's own deadline, generally between October and January
documents: Bachelor's degree certificate or proof of being in the final year of bachelor's studies
Consortium-specific admission documents listed on the chosen master's website
application_method: Search the Erasmus Mundus course catalogue for the latest selected masters
Contact the consortium and apply directly to the institution running the programme
Apply for the scholarship through the same consortium application, following each master's published steps
existing.selection_notes: A new batch of selected Erasmus Mundus Masters is added to the list each year. Each master's own website has the full application steps, entry requirements and selection arrangements; the Erasmus Mundus Association (em-a.eu) publishes applicant advice.
existing.best_fit: Graduates of a bachelor's degree, from any country, seeking an integrated master's programme delivered across at least three countries who can apply in the October-to-January window ahead of the following academic year.
existing.notes: This row is scoped to Belgian host institutions via the Wallonie-Bruxelles Campus portal studyinbelgium.be. That portal returned HTTP 429 on two attempts on 2026-10-04, so the Belgian participating institutions could not be listed from the awarding body's own European Commission pages; consult the consortium websites for the actual Belgian offerings.
existing.application_period: Each consortium sets its own deadlines; the European Commission states that in most cases applications are submitted between October and January for courses starting the following academic year.
existing.deadline_display: In most cases you should submit your application between October and January for courses starting the following academic year. Deadlines are set by each individual consortium.
